title: Three Layouts
subtitle: One program builds every gallery layout at once, and the worst quality gauge picks the winner

chapters.title: Three Layouts at Once
chapters.blurb: A Handwired gallery cannot skip work, so it builds Cinema, Contact sheet and Story for twelve photos on every frame.
captions: When a gallery's window resizes, twelve photos need a layout. But a Handwired program is fixed weighted sums and relu, which zeroes negatives. It cannot skip work the way an if statement does.
So this lab builds all the answers. On every frame it computes three complete layouts, and only afterwards decides which one to show.
Cinema is a hero photo with a rail of thumbnails beside it, two columns wide. The hero is the photo in focus.
The Contact sheet has no hero: twelve equal thumbnails in four columns and three rows. Story lays the hero across the top, with thumbnails below in three columns.
Positions are sums of the stage's width, its height and a 14 pixel gap, with clamps along the way. A Contact cell's width is the width minus five gaps, divided by four.
On a 1,400 by 680 stage, that makes a Contact cell 332 and a half pixels wide and 208 tall.
Cinema caps its rail at 280 pixels, leaving a hero 1,078 by 652. Story's hero is 394 tall, so its thumbnails get just over 50 pixels of height.
Drag the stage narrower and every number slides along. Where a subtraction would go negative, a relu pins it at zero, so even a 20 pixel sliver gets finite sizes.
Nothing is chosen yet. All three layouts, plus the click and focus logic, are 417 operations in 60 layers, and every frame computes every one.
Building every answer is the price of having no branch. The next question is how to pick one.

chapters.title: The Worst Gauge Wins
chapters.blurb: Each layout is scored by its smallest quality gauge, and a tournament of two comparisons lights a single one-hot bit.
captions: A layout is good when its pieces are big enough to see. Each size gets a gauge: the size times a scale, one over a target size, capped at 1.
A Contact cell targets 240 pixels. At 1,400 by 680 its width gauge is full, but its 208 pixel height reads 0.87.
Cinema's four gauges all read 1 there. Story's thumbnails are 50 tall against a target of 60, so its weakest gauge reads 0.84.
A layout is only as good as its worst gauge, so its score is the smallest one. A minimum is the smaller number minus a relu of the difference.
The picker, argmax, compares two scores at a time: Cinema against Contact, then the survivor against Story. A bias one float step above a half sends exact ties left.
What leaves the tournament is a one-hot: a 1 for the winner, a 0 for each loser. Here that is 1, 0, 0, and Cinema wins with a score of 1.
Narrow to 984 by 730. Cinema's hero shrinks to 666 pixels against a 900 target, so its gauge falls to 0.74. Contact wins, 0.94 over Story's 0.93.
At 610 by 830, Contact's cells are 135 wide, a gauge of 0.56. Its height gauge is a perfect 1, but only the worst gauge counts.
Story's hero is 439 tall against a 440 target, and its other gauges are full. Story scores 0.998 and takes over.
The flip is tight. At 517 tall, 760 wide picks Contact, but at 600 wide Story wins, 0.555 against 0.552. A three-way tie, as at 1,280 by 800, goes to Cinema.

chapters.title: Everyone Reads the Winner
chapters.blurb: The one-hot multiplies every layout's geometry and sums, so twelve thumbnails and the hero follow the winner, and clicks follow them.
captions: The winner is just a 1 and two 0s. Twelve thumbnails and a hero still need rectangles, and they get them by multiplication, not an if.
Take thumbnail zero's left edge. Each layout offers a value; multiply each by its own bit and add. Two of the three products are multiplied by zero.
On the 1,400 by 680 stage, the sum is Cinema's rectangle: left 1,106, top 14, 133 wide, 97 tall. The other two layouts were computed too, then erased by zero.
Every thumbnail and the hero run the same four sums. The Contact sheet has no hero, so its hero flag is zero.
At 984 by 730 the bit moves to Contact and thumbnail zero flies to the corner. At 610 by 830 it moves to Story and drops below the hero.
Declared a one-hot, these products lower to gather reads: 26 in one group, and the stored weights fall from 940 to 848.
A click uses the same rectangles. Each thumbnail turns the click's distance from its nearest edge into a bit, and the first hit sets that photo's focus cell to 1.
At 1,400 by 680, a click one pixel inside thumbnail seven hits it. A quarter pixel inside misses, and focus stays put.
The tests count exactly 14 rounding points: twelve thumbnail hit tests and two argmax comparisons. The rest is plain arithmetic.
The status is plain: a working demo, moved into the lab folder on September 17, 2026, and a subject of runtime cost measurements. Nothing is learned; the scales are written by hand.
So the program never branches. It builds every layout, scores each by its worst gauge, and multiplies the losers by zero, every frame.
